recipes.name: Mom's Best Ham and Bean Soup
ingredients_raw: 0.25 teaspoon cracked black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Place dry beans into a saucepan and add water to cover by one inch. Bring to a boil, then remove from the heat, cover, and let stand for 1 hour. Drain and rinse beans.

Pour 3 cups fresh water into a large pressure cooker. Add drained beans and ham bone, then stir in parsley, onion flakes, garlic, bay leaves, thyme, dry mustard, chili powder, and paprika. Seal the pressure cooker and heat to 15 pounds per square inch. Cook under pressure for 7 minutes; add 1 minute for every 1,000 feet above sea level. Remove from the heat and allow pressure to subside naturally.

When the pressure has reduced, open the lid. Stir in 5 cups water, tomato purée, celery, ketchup, chicken soup base, molasses, olive oil, brown sugar, and cracked black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Simmer until beans are tender, about 45 minutes. Stir in shell pasta and simmer until tender, about 15 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Best Ham and Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: This family-favorite navy bean soup is simple to make in a pressure cooker. It's a hearty mix of beans and pasta in a sweet, savory, and spicy broth.

review.reviewBody: This was a very good and versitile recipe. I made it twice in a week. First time I used lg lima beans, a smoked turkey leg and chopped up plum tomatoes turned out great. I shared it with my friends and family. Second time was because my daughter's boyfriend & mother-in-law brought home a ham bone from Easter and ask that I make them some soup like I made the first time. Everyone loved it. Thank your mom for sharing and thank you for posting it. Im sure I will be making it for years to come. YUMMY =]

This recipe is delicious. I don't have a pressure cooker so I made it the old fashion way, a pot on the stove, and it turned out just fine. The ham bone is what really gave this recipe its depth of flavor. Next time I make it I will reduce the amount of ketchup because I did find it a bit too sweet.

I had soaked my beans overnight so I had no need to boil them first. I had no celery but had everything else. I threw it ALL in the pressure cooker including all the tomato (I used large can of sauce). I did use chunks of a ham cut up, but no ham bone. It all went in the pressure cooker. It was very good! I'd make it like this again!

Excellent soup! I pressure cooked the beans and ham hock then threw the rest in the slow cooker on LOW for about 6 hours. Added pasta in the last 1/2 hour or so. It was savory and delicious and even better the 2nd day! Will definitely make this again. Even the bean soup critics at my house LOVED it!

I used leftover spiral glazed ham, did not include the celery and used canned beans ... and it was fast AND delicious! All of this spices (which I happened to have had on hand) created a very tasty soup!
REALLY GOOD was the rating from my picky eater. I used canned beans and the crock pot, however, followed the rest of the recipe.

This was a great soup. I don't have a pressure cooker so I used a can of pinto beans and cooked it for several hours on the stove. It's a very versatile recipe that can be tweaked. I may add a few diced potatoes next time. Tastes even better the next day!
Did not have tomato puree, so I used spaghetti sauce I had in fridge. Otherwise I used ingredients listed. This soup is full of flavor and was immensely enjoyed by all.

I'm not a bean fan. I ate 3 bowls of this. I had no brown sugar and molasses after I got started, so I used BBQ sauce and a dash of worshershire sauce. If you have kids that fight you on eating beans at least give this a try.

Was scouring the web looking for a tomato based soup and I stumbled on this and was elated. I had my Christmas Ham Bone and every other ingredient in my pantry. I made it to recipe except entirely in the pressure cooker. OMG it was so yummy and I loved the rich broth. I will make this everytime I have a Ham Bone and probably even when I don't Great recipe!
Was really good and my family loved it! Will be making this soup again!

I don't have a pressure cooker so I had to adjust the recipe somewhat to make sure the beans were cooked. I have made this many times and love it. I like that it is somewhat sweet...and if you want more ham flavor , add diced ham to it, a great use for leftovers.

Made according to directions except for using no pressure cooker and 2 ham hocks, I did not like it although I had been hankering for something that sounds like this. It was too sweet and too tomatoey for me. Even with the extra ham hock, I couldn't taste the ham. If you want something that reminds you of a ketchupy meatloaf this might do. Out of 4 diners, we had three votes for 2-stars and one for 4. Now she has three lunches.

I didn't have a pressure cooker so I made this in the crockpot, which of course took much longer, but I anticipated that and I didn't use the last 5 cups of water because there was no need. I thought it was too sweet. My husband even commented on it and added parmesan to his bowl. I don't think I'll be making this again.

Great flavor, the beans cooked perfectly. For our family it was too tomatoey for our liking (reminiscent of campbells tomato soup but with fresh ingredients and flavors). Good recipe, thanks for sharing.
